headline: Phylogeny-aware and structure-aware tools link microbial genes to phenotypes
label: Metagenomic And Pangenome Analysis Tools
summary: Recent preprints and publications introduce phylogeny-, graph- and structure-aware methods for gene-level inference from metagenomes and genomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is gene-level inference that accounts for evolutionary or structural context rather than treating genes as independent features. The robust permutation test and Phylogenize2 incorporate phylogenetic structure into gene-to-abundance association across host-associated and environmental microbiomes, with Phylogenize2 drawing on MGnify and GlobDB genome collections. DiscERN classifies biosynthetic gene clusters by Pfam content, homology and predicted structure, and AlphaGEM combines proteome-scale structural alignment with deep-learning mining of dark metabolic reactions to build genome-scale metabolic models. The remaining entries are heterogeneous: a Pseudomonas cross-strain iModulon analysis using ICA of RNA-seq data, a proteome-wide M. leprae pooled-AlphaFold3 interaction prediction, and microbial single-cell transcriptomics of mouse gut contents. What is new is the integration of phylogeny and predicted structure into tools that extend gene-level discovery.
